fields.explanation: A Schemaxis workflow (version schemaxis.workflow/1): an ordered list of operations, each embedding one complete adaptor document (ParaView, FreeCAD, Gmsh, Octave, ...), plus optional shared authoring context (dimensions, definitions, settings), study axes and resource budgets. Operations pass data to later operations only through verified producer outputs ($artifact files or $value results); native objects never cross between operations. Without execution settings or $value result references, operations run one after another in list order; otherwise the scheduler starts each operation once its producers are verified and its reservation fits the budget.
pitfalls: A successful host plan does not prove that an artifact index exists or that its kind suits the consumer; both are rechecked against the producer receipt during execution.
Workflow-level axes or analytics make the whole workflow a finite study: every operation runs once per state, so total run time grows with the number of states.

/properties/version.explanation: Fixed identifier of the workflow envelope contract. It is an input-format version, not an application version; each embedded operation document keeps its own version (for example schemaxis.gmsh/1).
/properties/version.label: Workflow version
/properties/version.defaultMeaning: Required; any other value fails with UNSUPPORTED_VERSION.
pitfalls: Do not put an adaptor version such as schemaxis/1 here; it belongs in operations[].document.version.

/properties/execution.explanation: Workflow-wide resource budget for the scheduler: how many native jobs may run at once and the CPU slots, declared memory and GPU slots they may reserve together. Including this object, even empty, switches the workflow from serial execution in list order to scheduled execution, in which independent operations can overlap. Each operation's own execution reservation must fit within this budget or planning fails with RESOURCE_BUDGET_EXCEEDED.
/properties/execution.label: Execution budget
/properties/execution.defaultMeaning: Omitted: serial execution in list order, unless $value result references or a scheduled route enable the scheduler; it then uses maxWorkers 1, cpus = host logical CPU count, memoryMB 8192 and gpus 1.
pitfalls: Memory and CPU values are admission estimates, not operating-system limits; set them from measured consumption with headroom for other applications.

/properties/execution/properties/maxWork.explanation: Maximum number of native jobs (operation batches) the scheduler runs at the same time. Higher values let independent operations or time batches overlap, but every running job must still fit the shared cpus, memoryMB and gpus budget, so actual concurrency can be lower.
/properties/execution/properties/maxWork.label: Maximum concurrent jobs
/properties/execution/properties/maxWork.defaultMeaning: Scheduler default: 1 (one job at a time).
pitfalls: Raising maxWorkers alone adds no parallelism when operations depend on each other or their reservations already use up cpus or memoryMB.

/properties/execution/properties/cpus.explanation: Total CPU slots shared by concurrently running jobs. Each job reserves threads x ranks slots; jobs wait while the remaining slots are insufficient, and a job that alone needs more than this total fails planning with RESOURCE_BUDGET_EXCEEDED.
/properties/execution/properties/cpus.label: CPU slots
/properties/execution/properties/cpus.defaultMeaning: Scheduler default: the host's logical CPU count.
pitfalls: This is an admission budget, not CPU affinity or a cgroup limit.

/properties/execution/properties/memoryM.explanation: Total declared RAM that concurrently running jobs may reserve together. Each operation reserves its own execution.memoryMB for its whole job (all MPI ranks included); a job is admitted only while the sum of running reservations stays within this budget.
/properties/execution/properties/memoryM.label: Memory budget
pitfalls: Reservations are estimates used for admission; Schemaxis does not stop a job that uses more memory than it declared.

/properties/execution/properties/gpus.explanation: Number of GPU slots available to the scheduler; only 0 or 1 is supported. With 1, at most one GPU-reserving job (for example a CUDA or OptiX Blender render) runs at a time, which prevents simultaneous renders competing for one device. With 0, any operation that needs a GPU reservation cannot fit the budget.
/properties/execution/properties/gpus.label: GPU slots
pitfalls: Multi-GPU device assignment is not supported; values above 1 fail with UNSUPPORTED_EXECUTION.

/properties/operations.explanation: The ordered workflow steps. Each entry wraps one complete adaptor document under an ID that later references use ($artifact, $value with path, and $document with operation). A producer must appear before every operation that consumes its outputs; forward and self references are rejected. In serial mode the list order is the execution order; in scheduled mode it is only a valid dependency order and unrelated operations can overlap.
/properties/operations.label: Operations
/properties/operations.defaultMeaning: Required; at least one operation (EMPTY_WORKFLOW otherwise).
pitfalls: Moving a consumer above its producer fails with UNAVAILABLE_OPERATION even if the data flow is otherwise correct.
Operation IDs must be unique (DUPLICATE_OPERATION).

/properties/operations/items.explanation: One workflow step: an ID, the embedded adaptor document it runs, and optional per-job resource reservations. The document is planned and executed by its own adaptor in an isolated native process; only verified published files and values reach later steps.

/properties/operations/items/properties/.explanation: Name of this step, unique within the workflow. Later steps refer to it in {"$artifact": id, "index": n}, {"$value": id, "path": ...} and {"$document": ..., "operation": id}; it also names the step's run directory and its scheduled jobs (id/batch). It starts with a letter, followed by letters, digits, underscores or hyphens.
/properties/operations/items/properties/.label: Operation ID
pitfalls: Renaming an operation breaks every reference to it; update those references in the same edit.

/properties/operations/items/properties/.explanation: The complete input document of one workflow-capable adaptor route, for example schemaxis/1 (ParaView), schemaxis.freecad/1, schemaxis.gmsh/1 or schemaxis.octave/1. Its version selects the adaptor and its contents follow that adaptor's own schema and help. It may contain $artifact and $value references to earlier operations, which are resolved only after the producer has been verified.
/properties/operations/items/properties/.label: Adaptor document
pitfalls: Standalone-only document versions are rejected inside a workflow with UNSUPPORTED_PROVIDER; run them directly.
An absolute $document pointer inside this document stays local to it; add "scope": "workflow" to read the workflow's dimensions, definitions or settings.

/properties/operations/items/properties/.explanation: Resources this operation's job reserves from the workflow execution budget, plus optional MPI and time-batch settings. The scheduler admits the job only when its threads x ranks CPU slots, memoryMB and gpus all fit what remains. Adding it to any operation also switches the workflow to scheduled execution.
/properties/operations/items/properties/.label: Job reservation
/properties/operations/items/properties/.defaultMeaning: Omitted: threads from the adaptor's resource rule (otherwise 1), ranks 1, memoryMB 1024, gpus as the adaptor requires (1 for GPU renders, otherwise 0), and no time splitting.

/properties/operations/items/properties/.explanation: Threads per MPI rank (ParaView) or per Blender process; the job reserves threads x ranks CPU slots. It constrains common OpenMP, BLAS and VTK thread pools; for Blender renders it must match the document's render.threads.
/properties/operations/items/properties/.label: Threads per process
/properties/operations/items/properties/.defaultMeaning: From the adaptor's resource rule where one exists (for example Blender render threads); otherwise 1.
pitfalls: Thread settings are not CPU affinity; check that threads x ranks fits the workflow cpus budget.

/properties/operations/items/properties/.explanation: Number of MPI processes for this operation. Values above 1 launch ParaView as mpiexec -n N pvbatch and require an absolute mpiexec path; only adaptors with an MPI execution mode (currently ParaView, for a qualified subset of operations) accept it. The job reserves ranks x threads CPU slots.
/properties/operations/items/properties/.label: MPI ranks
pitfalls: Other adaptors fail with UNSUPPORTED_EXECUTION; unqualified ParaView operations are rejected before MPI dispatch.
Use the mpiexec that belongs to the MPI installation ParaView was built against.

/properties/operations/items/properties/.explanation: Declared RAM for this operation's whole job, including all MPI ranks, deducted from the workflow memoryMB budget while the job runs.
/properties/operations/items/properties/.label: Memory reservation
pitfalls: This is an admission estimate, not a limit. Base it on a previous run's metrics file (sampled RSS) plus headroom.

/properties/operations/items/properties/.explanation: GPU slots this job reserves. Adaptors that render on a GPU (Blender with CUDA or OptiX) require at least 1, and a smaller value fails with INVALID_EXECUTION; the reservation must also fit the workflow gpus budget, which allows at most one.
/properties/operations/items/properties/.label: GPU reservation
/properties/operations/items/properties/.defaultMeaning: As the adaptor requires: 1 for CUDA/OptiX renders, otherwise 0.

/properties/operations/items/properties/.explanation: Splits this operation's explicit times list into independent jobs of at most this many consecutive timesteps, which can run concurrently. Each batch keeps the full analytic sweep and native object reuse within its own process; artifacts are concatenated in batch order, so $artifact indices do not depend on completion order.
/properties/operations/items/properties/.label: Timesteps per batch
/properties/operations/items/properties/.defaultMeaning: No splitting: the whole operation runs as one job.
pitfalls: Requires a document route that supports time batches and a finite, explicit times list; source-time discovery cannot be split (UNSUPPORTED_BATCH).
A downstream operation waits for all of the producer's batches, not for individual early artifacts.

/properties/operations/items/properties/.explanation: Conditional MPI rule: when ranks is 2 or more, mpiexec becomes required and must be an absolute path (a string starting with /). Serial jobs (ranks omitted or 1) do not need it.
Condition of the MPI rule: it matches when ranks is present and at least 2, i.e. when the job will start several MPI processes.
Threshold of the MPI rule: a ranks value of 2 or more makes the requirement for an absolute mpiexec path apply.
Requirement applied to MPI jobs: mpiexec must be present and be an absolute launcher path.

Absolute path of the mpiexec launcher used to start this operation's MPI ranks. Choose the launcher of the MPI installation that ParaView was built against; Schemaxis does not search PATH for it, and the native receipt must report the requested rank count.
/properties/operations/items/properties/.label: MPI launcher
pitfalls: A bare name such as "mpiexec" fails with INVALID_EXECUTION; give the full path.

/properties/maxStates.explanation: Upper bound on the number of states (visits) a finite study may expand to: the product of the lengths of all independent axes and unsynchronized analytic sequences. Exceeding it fails before any native work with EXPANSION_TOO_LARGE; it also caps the length of each axis and analytic sequence.
/properties/maxStates.label: Maximum states
/properties/maxStates.defaultMeaning: 10000, which is also the largest allowed value.
pitfalls: Each workflow-level state reruns the whole workflow; a lower maxStates catches an accidental Cartesian product before it runs.

/properties/axes.explanation: Explicit workflow-level sweep axes. Each entry needs a distinct name and exactly one of values (a nonempty list) or series (a linear series given by three of start, end, spacing and count). Independent axes form a Cartesian product of states and the whole workflow runs once per state. {"$axis": name} markers in the workflow's dimensions, definitions or settings read the current value; operations reach them with {"$document": ..., "scope": "workflow"}.
/properties/axes.label: Study axes
pitfalls: Workflow axes and each operation document's own axes have separate name scopes; an $axis inside an operation document only sees that document's axes (UNKNOWN_AXIS).
An entry with both values and series, or neither, fails with INVALID_AXIS.

/$defs/json.explanation: Any plain JSON value: null, a boolean, a finite number, a string, or arrays and objects of these. The schema uses it where it accepts arbitrary data, for example the samples of an $analytic values list; whether the value is meaningful is decided by the code that consumes it.
pitfalls: NaN and Infinity are not JSON and are rejected when the document is loaded.

/$defs/json/anyOf/0.explanation: A single scalar: null, true or false, a number or a string. Choose it for one value rather than a list or object.

/$defs/json/anyOf/1.explanation: A JSON array whose elements are arbitrary JSON values, including nested arrays and objects.

/$defs/json/anyOf/2.explanation: A JSON object with string keys and arbitrary JSON member values.

/$defs/documentReference.explanation: A $document marker: replaces this whole value with a copy of the JSON found at a pointer, so one authored value can be reused in several places. Absolute pointers (/...) address the current document; ./ and ../ paths start from the object or array that contains the marker. In a workflow, add operation to read another operation's authored document, or scope "workflow" to read the workflow envelope.
pitfalls: It copies authored input, never results: it does not wait for or read native output. Use $value with path or $artifact for verified results.
Missing targets, malformed ~ escapes, relative paths above the root and reference cycles fail.

/$defs/documentReference/properties/$doc.explanation: JSON pointer (RFC 6901) to the value to copy. /a/b starts at the root of the current document (inside an operation document, that document unless operation or scope says otherwise); ./x and ../x start from the object or array containing this marker, where it was written. Array members use zero-based indices (/nodes/0/options/radius); inside a key, ~1 stands for / and ~0 for ~.
/$defs/documentReference/properties/$doc.label: Pointer
pitfalls: Pointer parts are exact key names; a typo never yields null. Inside a standalone or operation document a missing target fails with UNKNOWN_DOCUMENT_REFERENCE; a workflow-scope or operation form that selects a missing value fails with UNKNOWN_REFERENCE.

/$defs/documentReference/properties/oper.explanation: Workflow only: ID of another operation whose authored document the pointer addresses, for example to reuse a FreeCAD thickness as a Gmsh size. The pointer must then be absolute. It reads authored input, so the source operation does not have to run first and no execution dependency is created; the workflow diagram shows it as a document-reference edge.
/$defs/documentReference/properties/oper.label: Source operation
pitfalls: Cannot be combined with scope; an unknown operation or relative pointer fails with UNKNOWN_DOCUMENT_REFERENCE.

/$defs/documentReference/properties/scop.explanation: Workflow only: "workflow" makes an absolute pointer start at the workflow envelope instead of the current operation document, so operations can share /dimensions, /definitions and /settings declared once. Studio writes this form when you expose an operation value as a template parameter.
/$defs/documentReference/properties/scop.label: Scope
/$defs/documentReference/properties/scop.defaultMeaning: Omitted: an absolute pointer inside an operation document stays local to that document.
pitfalls: Only "workflow" is accepted, and it cannot be combined with operation.

/$defs/numericTree.explanation: Endpoint of a linear $analytic sequence: a single finite number, or a nonempty (possibly nested) array of numbers such as an XYZ point. Both endpoints of one sequence must have the same shape, because samples are interpolated component by component.

/$defs/numericTree/anyOf/0.explanation: Scalar endpoint; choose it to sweep one number such as a size, offset or angle.

/$defs/numericTree/anyOf/1.explanation: Array endpoint; choose it to sweep a point or vector, for example [0, 0, 2]. The other endpoint must have the same length and nesting.

/$defs/numericTree/anyOf/1/items.explanation: One component of the array endpoint: a number, a nested array, or a composition marker that evaluates to one.

/$defs/analytic.explanation: An $analytic marker: replaces this value with a generated finite sequence and makes the document a scheduled study with one state (visit) per sample. values lists samples explicitly, linear interpolates between two endpoints, and orbit produces a camera list. Sequences sharing a sync name advance together; independent ones combine as a Cartesian product, limited by maxStates.
pitfalls: Place analytics only where the route evaluates them (node option values, dimensions/definitions/settings, image camera lists and appearances); do not assume an analytic placed elsewhere is evaluated.
The wrapper may contain only $analytic.

/$defs/analytic/properties/$analytic.explanation: The sequence definition. Its type selects values, linear or orbit, each with its own keys; in successive states this field takes successive samples (orbit instead supplies its whole camera list at once).
/$defs/analytic/properties/$analytic.label: Sequence

/$defs/analytic/properties/$analytic/any.explanation: Explicit list of samples. Choose it when the values are irregular, non-numeric (strings, objects, file names) or already known, for example [0.5, 1, 2]; each state receives the next element unchanged.
Selects the explicit-list sequence: samples are taken from values in order.
/$defs/analytic/properties/$analytic/any.label: Sequence type

/$defs/analytic/properties/$analytic/any.explanation: Nonempty ordered list of samples; element i is used in state i of this sequence. Elements may be any JSON, including markers that are resolved in each state. The list length counts towards maxStates.
/$defs/analytic/properties/$analytic/any.label: Samples
pitfalls: An empty list fails with EMPTY_ANALYTIC; one longer than maxStates fails with EXPANSION_TOO_LARGE.

/$defs/analytic/properties/$analytic/any.explanation: One sample: a JSON value used as-is in one state, or a composition marker evaluated in that state.

Name that synchronizes this explicit list with every values or linear sequence carrying the same sync name: they advance together (zipped) instead of multiplying into a Cartesian product. All members of a group must have the same length.
/$defs/analytic/properties/$analytic/any.label: Sync group
/$defs/analytic/properties/$analytic/any.defaultMeaning: Unsynchronized: this list is an independent axis multiplied with all others.
pitfalls: Members of one group with different lengths fail with ANALYTIC_LENGTH_MISMATCH.

/$defs/analytic/properties/$analytic/any.explanation: Evenly spaced samples from start to end, both included. Choose it for numeric sweeps of a scalar or of a point or vector (interpolated per component); for example count 3 from [0, 0, 0] to [0, 0, 2] gives [0, 0, 0], [0, 0, 1] and [0, 0, 2].
Selects linear interpolation between start and end.
/$defs/analytic/properties/$analytic/any.label: Sequence type

/$defs/analytic/properties/$analytic/any.explanation: First sample of the linear sequence. A finite number, or an array of numbers with exactly the same shape as end.
/$defs/analytic/properties/$analytic/any.label: Start

/$defs/analytic/properties/$analytic/any.explanation: Last sample of the linear sequence (reached when count is greater than 1). Same shape as start.
/$defs/analytic/properties/$analytic/any.label: End
pitfalls: With count 1, end must equal start (INVALID_ANALYTIC).

/$defs/analytic/properties/$analytic/any.explanation: Number of samples including both endpoints; the step is (end - start)/(count - 1). At least 1 and at most maxStates.
/$defs/analytic/properties/$analytic/any.label: Sample count

/$defs/analytic/properties/$analytic/any.explanation: Name that synchronizes this linear sweep with other values or linear sequences of the same sync name, so they advance together (for example a position and a matching label) instead of forming a Cartesian product.
/$defs/analytic/properties/$analytic/any.label: Sync group
pitfalls: Every member of the group needs the same number of samples (ANALYTIC_LENGTH_MISMATCH).

/$defs/analytic/properties/$analytic/any.explanation: Camera orbit: evenly spaced azimuths from start to end (degrees, both included), each converted to a camera object {direction, up} at the given elevation with +z as up. It replaces the whole value with the camera list, so use it for an image writer's cameras value, not for a scalar angle or an XYZ option.
pitfalls: start 0 and end 360 give the same view twice; for N distinct views around a full turn use end = 360 x (N - 1)/N.
orbit does not accept sync, and it supplies only direction and up; use the orbitCameras function for framed cameras.

/$defs/analytic/properties/$analytic/any.explanation: Selects the orbit camera sequence.
/$defs/analytic/properties/$analytic/any.label: Sequence type

/$defs/analytic/properties/$analytic/any.explanation: Azimuth of the first camera, measured in the x-y plane from +x towards +y (anticlockwise seen from +z).
/$defs/analytic/properties/$analytic/any.label: Start azimuth

/$defs/analytic/properties/$analytic/any.explanation: Azimuth of the last camera, reached when count is greater than 1; intermediate azimuths are evenly spaced.
/$defs/analytic/properties/$analytic/any.label: End azimuth

/$defs/analytic/properties/$analytic/any.explanation: Number of cameras, including both end azimuths; at least 1 and at most maxStates.
/$defs/analytic/properties/$analytic/any.label: Camera count

/$defs/analytic/properties/$analytic/any.explanation: Angle of every camera above (positive) or below (negative) the x-y plane; strictly between -90 and 90.
/$defs/analytic/properties/$analytic/any.label: Elevation

/$defs/valueReference.explanation: Workflow result reference ($value with path): replaces this value with data selected from a verified result of an earlier operation, for example a measured volume reused as a later mesh size. The scheduler waits for the producer, verifies its receipt and artifacts, selects the value, then validates and runs the consumer. It is distinct from $value with args, which calls a registered function.
pitfalls: The producer must appear earlier in operations; forward and self references fail with UNAVAILABLE_OPERATION.
Units are not inferred from numbers; keep the producer's documented units or convert explicitly with $expr.

/$defs/valueReference/properties/$value.explanation: ID of the earlier operation whose verified output is read. The reference creates a dependency and switches the workflow to scheduled execution.
/$defs/valueReference/properties/$value.label: Producer operation

/$defs/valueReference/properties/path.explanation: RFC 6901 pointer into the selected JSON: into the producer's verified receipt when artifact is omitted, or into the chosen JSON or numeric CSV artifact when it is given (CSV tables expose columns and rows, e.g. /rows/0/1). An empty string selects the whole value.
/$defs/valueReference/properties/path.label: Result pointer
pitfalls: Inspect the producer's actual verified receipt or artifact before choosing a pointer; result keys differ between adaptors.

/$defs/valueReference/properties/visit.explanation: Zero-based index of the producer's visit (state) to read when the producer itself ran several states.
/$defs/valueReference/properties/visit.label: Producer visit
pitfalls: A multi-visit producer needs an explicit visit unless the enclosing workflow study provides one producer execution per state.

/$defs/valueReference/properties/artifac.explanation: Zero-based index, in the producer's verified artifact order, of a JSON or numeric CSV publication to read before path is applied. Extraction is bounded to 8 MiB.
/$defs/valueReference/properties/artifac.label: Artifact index
/$defs/valueReference/properties/artifac.defaultMeaning: Omitted: path selects from the producer's verified native receipt instead.

/$defs/axisReference.explanation: An $axis marker: replaces this value with the current state's value of a declared axis, optionally narrowed by path. Use it to drive several fields from one explicit axis instead of writing separate analytics.
pitfalls: The axis must be declared in the same scope: markers at workflow level see workflow axes, markers inside an operation document see only that document's axes (UNKNOWN_AXIS).

/$defs/axisReference/properties/$axis.explanation: Name of an axis declared in the axes list of the current scope.
/$defs/axisReference/properties/$axis.label: Axis name

/$defs/axisReference/properties/path.explanation: Keys and zero-based indices applied in order to select part of the axis value; for example ["position", 2] selects the third (z) component of a position member. A missing member fails with UNKNOWN_REFERENCE.
/$defs/axisReference/properties/path.label: Member path

/$defs/axisReference/properties/path/ite.explanation: One step of the member path: an object key (string) or a zero-based array index (integer).
Object-key step; use it when the value reached so far is an object.
Array-index step (zero-based); use it when the value reached so far is a list.

/$defs/authorNumber.explanation: Numeric operand of an authored expression: a literal number, or a composition marker or $analytic that produces one. Booleans do not count as numbers.
pitfalls: A marker resolving to a non-number fails when the expression is evaluated, not when the document is parsed.

/$defs/authorNumber/anyOf/0.explanation: Literal number; choose it when the operand is known while authoring.

/$defs/authorString.explanation: String operand (used by concat, omit key lists and namedGet): a literal string, or a marker or $analytic that produces one.

/$defs/authorString/anyOf/0.explanation: Literal string; choose it for a fixed name or text fragment.

/$defs/authorArray.explanation: Array operand (used by concat and get): a literal array whose elements may contain markers, or a marker or $analytic that produces an array.

/$defs/authorArray/anyOf/0.explanation: Literal array; its elements are authored values that may themselves contain markers.

/$defs/authorObject.explanation: Object operand (used by merge, overlay, omit and get): a literal object whose member values may contain markers, or a marker or $analytic that produces an object.
pitfalls: An object whose own keys include $document, $expr or $value is read as that marker, not as plain data.

/$defs/authorObject/anyOf/0.explanation: Literal object operand. It cannot itself carry $document, $expr or $value keys, because such an object is the corresponding marker; its member values may still be markers.

/$defs/authorObject/anyOf/0/not.explanation: Exclusion rule for object operands: an object with $document, $expr or $value at its own top level is a marker and must match that marker's definition instead of being treated as plain data.

/$defs/authorObject/anyOf/0/not/anyOf/0.explanation: Excludes object operands that contain $document (a document reference).

/$defs/authorObject/anyOf/0/not/anyOf/1.explanation: Excludes object operands that contain $expr (an expression).

/$defs/authorObject/anyOf/0/not/anyOf/2.explanation: Excludes object operands that contain $value (a function call or result reference).

/$defs/authorData.explanation: Any authored JSON value in which markers may appear at any depth: scalars, arrays, plain objects or a composition marker ($document, $expr, $value, $axis). It is the type of the workflow dimensions, definitions and settings and of axes entries.

/$defs/authorData/anyOf/0.explanation: Literal scalar: null, true or false, a number or a string.

/$defs/authorData/anyOf/1.explanation: Array of authored values; each element may contain markers.

/$defs/authorData/anyOf/2.explanation: Plain object of authored values (an $analytic object also has this shape). An object whose own keys include $document, $expr or $value is a marker instead.

/$defs/authorData/anyOf/2/not.explanation: Exclusion rule for plain authored objects: $document, $expr or $value at the top level makes the object a marker, validated by the composition definition.

/$defs/authorData/anyOf/2/not/anyOf/0.explanation: Excludes plain objects that contain $document; those are document references.

/$defs/authorData/anyOf/2/not/anyOf/1.explanation: Excludes plain objects that contain $expr; those are expressions.

/$defs/authorData/anyOf/2/not/anyOf/2.explanation: Excludes plain objects that contain $value; those are function calls or result references.

/$defs/expression.explanation: Body of an $expr marker: one closed operation (op) on exactly two arguments (args), plus an optional conflict policy for merge and namedMerge. Arguments may themselves contain markers; the result replaces the whole $expr value and keeps its JSON type. Operations: add, subtract, multiply, divide (scalars); merge, overlay, omit, get (objects and lists); concat (strings or arrays); namedMerge, namedGet (collections of named objects).
pitfalls: Always exactly two arguments; nest expressions for longer sums or products.
Authored arithmetic accepts scalar numbers only; for vector arithmetic during a graph visit use $calc.

/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/0.explanation: Scalar sum of two finite numbers: [2, 3] gives 5. Use it, for example, to add a clearance to a referenced dimension.
pitfalls: Booleans, strings, vectors or a non-finite result fail with INVALID_EXPRESSION.

/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/0/proper.explanation: The two numbers to add, [left, right]. Each may be a literal number or a marker that resolves to one.
/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/0/proper.label: Operands

/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/0/proper.explanation: First number of the sum; a literal or a marker such as a referenced dimension.
Second number, added to the first; addition is symmetric, so the order does not change the result.

/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/1.explanation: Scalar difference of two finite numbers: [7, 2] gives 5 (first minus second).
pitfalls: Booleans, strings, vectors or a non-finite result fail with INVALID_EXPRESSION.

/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/1/proper.explanation: The two numbers, [minuend, subtrahend]; the second is subtracted from the first. Each may be a literal number or a marker that resolves to one.
/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/1/proper.label: Operands

/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/2.explanation: Scalar product of two finite numbers: [2, 3] gives 6. Use it to scale a referenced dimension, for example a diameter from a radius.
pitfalls: Booleans, strings, vectors or a non-finite result fail with INVALID_EXPRESSION.

/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/2/proper.explanation: Operation name; "multiply" returns args[0] x args[1].
/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/2/proper.label: Operation

/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/2/proper.explanation: The two factors to multiply. Each may be a literal number or a marker that resolves to one.
/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/2/proper.label: Operands

/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/2/proper.explanation: First factor of the product; a literal or a marker resolving to a number.
Second factor of the product, for example a scale factor applied to the first.

/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/3.explanation: Scalar quotient of two finite numbers: [6, 2] gives 3 (first divided by second). Division by zero fails.
pitfalls: Booleans, strings, vectors or a non-finite result fail with INVALID_EXPRESSION.

/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/3/proper.explanation: The two numbers, [dividend, divisor]. Each may be a literal number or a marker that resolves to one.
/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/3/proper.label: Operands

/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/3/proper.explanation: Number to divide by (divisor); zero fails with INVALID_EXPRESSION.

/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/4.explanation: Recursive merge of two objects: nested objects are merged key by key, while arrays and scalars are atomic. When both sides hold different atomic values at the same place, conflict decides: left (default) keeps the first argument's value, right takes the second's, and error stops with COMPOSITION_CONFLICT. Example: [{"a": {"x": 1}}, {"a": {"y": 2}}] gives {"a": {"x": 1, "y": 2}}.
pitfalls: Unlike overlay, merge keeps the FIRST value on conflict by default; set conflict to "right" for override semantics.

/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/4/proper.explanation: Operation name; "merge" combines two objects recursively.
/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/4/proper.label: Operation

/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/4/proper.explanation: The two objects to merge, [base, other]; either may be supplied by a marker.
/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/4/proper.label: Operands

/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/4/proper.explanation: Base object; under the default conflict policy its atomic values win.
Object merged into the base: its new keys are added, nested objects merged, and its conflicting atomic values win only with conflict "right".

How merge resolves different atomic values (numbers, strings, booleans, null or arrays) at the same path: left keeps the first argument's value, right keeps the second's, error fails with COMPOSITION_CONFLICT and reports the location. Equal values never conflict; a boolean never equals a number.
/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/4/proper.label: Conflict policy
/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/4/proper.defaultMeaning: Schemaxis default: "left" (the first argument's value is kept where the two differ).

/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/5.explanation: Shallow overlay of two objects: the result has the top-level keys of both, and for shared keys the second object's value replaces the first's entirely (nested objects are replaced, not merged). Example: [{"a": 1}, {"a": 2, "b": 3}] gives {"a": 2, "b": 3}.
pitfalls: Use merge when nested objects should be combined rather than replaced.

/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/5/proper.explanation: Operation name; "overlay" replaces top-level keys of the first object with those of the second.
/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/5/proper.label: Operation

/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/5/proper.explanation: The base object and the overriding object, [base, override].
/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/5/proper.label: Operands

/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/5/proper.explanation: Base object; its keys are kept unless the second object also defines them.
Overriding object; each of its top-level keys replaces the base value as a whole.

/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/6.explanation: Copy of an object without some of its direct (top-level) keys: [{"a": 1, "b": 2}, ["a"]] gives {"b": 2}. Listed keys that are absent are ignored.

/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/6/proper.explanation: Operation name; "omit" removes direct keys from the first object.
/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/6/proper.label: Operation

/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/6/proper.explanation: The object to copy and the keys to drop, [object, keys].
/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/6/proper.label: Operands

/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/6/proper.explanation: Object to copy, minus the omitted keys.
Keys to drop: an array of key names, or an object whose keys are dropped (its values are ignored).
Array of key names to remove; choose it to list the keys explicitly.
One top-level key name to remove. It is a key, not a path: "a/b" removes a key literally named a/b.

/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/7.explanation: Joins two strings or two arrays end to end: ["mesh-", "fine"] gives "mesh-fine", [[1], [2]] gives [1, 2]. Both arguments must be of the same kind.
pitfalls: A string cannot be joined to a number; convert or build the text another way.

/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/7/proper.explanation: Operation name; "concat" appends the second string or array to the first.
/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/7/proper.label: Operation

/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/7/proper.explanation: Either two strings or two arrays, in the order they are joined.
/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/7/proper.label: Operands

/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/7/proper.explanation: String form: choose it to build a name, label or file stem from two parts.
Leading string; it appears first in the result.
Trailing string, appended directly after the first (no separator is added).
Array form: choose it to append the elements of one list to another; duplicates are kept.
Leading array; its elements come first in the result.
Array whose elements follow the first array's elements.

/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/8.explanation: Selects one direct member: an object key or a zero-based array index, e.g. [{"a": 1}, "a"] gives 1 and [[5, 6], 1] gives 6. Use it to pick one entry from a referenced table or list.
pitfalls: A missing key or out-of-range index fails with INVALID_EXPRESSION; there is no default value.

/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/8/proper.explanation: Operation name; "get" returns one member of an object or array.
/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/8/proper.label: Operation

/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/8/proper.explanation: The container and the member to read, [container, key or index].
/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/8/proper.label: Operands

/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/8/proper.explanation: Object or array to read from, often a $document or $value marker.
Key (string) for an object, or zero-based index (integer) for an array.
Zero-based array index; choose it when the first argument is an array.

/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/9.explanation: Merges two collections of named objects (arrays of objects, each with a unique nonempty name). Entries with the same name are merged recursively like merge, using conflict; names found only in the second collection are appended; the order of the first collection is kept. Useful for lists such as boundary patches or layers keyed by name.
pitfalls: Duplicate or empty names in either collection fail with INVALID_EXPRESSION.

/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/9/proper.explanation: Operation name; "namedMerge" merges two named collections by entry name.
/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/9/proper.label: Operation

/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/9/proper.explanation: The base collection and the collection merged into it.
/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/9/proper.label: Operands

/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/9/proper.explanation: Base collection; its order is preserved and its values win conflicts under the default policy.
One entry of the base collection: an object with a name plus any other members.
Nonempty name identifying this entry of the base collection; it must be unique within the collection and is how entries are matched.
/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/9/proper.label: Entry name

/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/9/proper.explanation: Any other member of an entry of the base collection; when the other collection has an entry of the same name, the two are merged recursively.
Collection merged into the base: same-named entries are merged, new names are appended in their order.
One entry of the collection merged into the base: an object with a name plus any other members.
Nonempty name identifying this entry of the collection merged into the base; it must be unique within the collection and is how entries are matched.
/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/9/proper.label: Entry name

/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/9/proper.explanation: Any other member of an entry of the collection merged into the base; it is merged into the same-named base entry, or copied with a new entry.
How unequal atomic values inside two same-named entries are resolved: left keeps the base value, right the second collection's, error fails with COMPOSITION_CONFLICT.
/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/9/proper.label: Conflict policy
/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/9/proper.defaultMeaning: Schemaxis default: "left" (the first argument's value is kept where the two differ).

/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/10.explanation: Selects the entry with a given name from a collection of named objects: [[{"name": "a", "x": 1}], "a"] gives {"name": "a", "x": 1}.
pitfalls: An absent name, or duplicate names in the collection, fail with INVALID_EXPRESSION.

/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/10/prope.explanation: Operation name; "namedGet" returns one entry of a named collection.
/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/10/prope.label: Operation

/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/10/prope.explanation: The collection to search and the name to find, [collection, name].
/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/10/prope.label: Operands

/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/10/prope.explanation: Named collection to search.
One entry of the collection searched by namedGet: an object with a name plus any other members.
Nonempty name identifying this entry of the collection searched by namedGet; it must be unique within the collection and is how entries are matched.
/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/10/prope.label: Entry name

/$defs/expression/anyOf/0/anyOf/10/prope.explanation: Any other member of an entry of the collection searched by namedGet; returned unchanged as part of the selected entry.
Name of the entry to return; it must exist in the collection.

/$defs/composition.explanation: Any authored composition marker that replaces a whole value before native execution: $document (copy authored JSON), $expr (closed operation), $value with args (registered pure function), $value with path (verified workflow result) or $axis (current axis value). The resolved value must still satisfy the destination field; markers are never interpolated inside strings.
pitfalls: A marker object may contain only its own keys; extra keys such as {"$document": ..., "default": 1} make it invalid.
Runtime graph markers ($observe, $sample, $calc, $call, $time) are separate and are not part of this union.

/$defs/composition/anyOf/1.explanation: Expression marker {"$expr": {"op": ..., "args": [...]}}: choose it to compute a value from other values (arithmetic, object merge/overlay/omit/get, concatenation, named collections). The wrapper may contain only $expr.

/$defs/composition/anyOf/2.explanation: Pure function call {"$value": name, "args": {...}}: choose it for geometric helpers (bounds centres and sizes, framing boxes, cameras, slice positions, direction vectors) computed from authored numbers. Only registered functions can be named; arguments are typed and validated, and the result type is checked.
pitfalls: When an argument depends on graph runtime data ($observe, $sample, $calc), use $call instead; $value is evaluated while authored input is prepared.
Exactly $value and args are allowed; path belongs to the workflow result form of $value.

/$defs/composition/anyOf/2/oneOf/0.explanation: Centre [x, y, z] of six-number VTK-order bounds [xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, zmin, zmax]; [0, 10, 0, 4, -1, 1] gives [5, 2, 0]. Choose it for bounds in ParaView's flat order; use boundsCentre3D for {min, max} boxes.
pitfalls: Any min greater than its max fails; zero thickness (min equal to max) is allowed, unlike boundsCentre3D.

/$defs/composition/anyOf/2/oneOf/0/prope.explanation: Registered function name; "boundsCentre" selects this calculation and fixes the argument and result contract.
/$defs/composition/anyOf/2/oneOf/0/prope.label: Function

/$defs/composition/anyOf/2/oneOf/0/prope.explanation: Arguments of boundsCentre: one required bounds array of six numbers. Usually a literal object; the whole object may also come from a marker (for example $document to shared arguments) or from an $analytic whose samples are complete argument objects.
/$defs/composition/anyOf/2/oneOf/0/prope.label: Arguments

/$defs/composition/anyOf/2/oneOf/0/prope.explanation: Literal argument object of boundsCentre: required bounds.
Six numbers in VTK order [xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, zmin, zmax]; each min must not exceed its max.
/$defs/composition/anyOf/2/oneOf/0/prope.label: Bounds
/$defs/composition/anyOf/2/oneOf/0/prope.units: Coordinate units of the data (no unit conversion)

/$defs/composition/anyOf/2/oneOf/0/prope.explanation: Literal six-number bounds array for boundsCentre; choose a marker to reuse bounds stored elsewhere.
One bound: positions 0-1 are xmin and xmax, 2-3 ymin and ymax, 4-5 zmin and zmax.
Literal number for one bound of boundsCentre. Choose a composition marker instead to compute it, or $analytic to sweep it across states.

/$defs/composition/anyOf/2/oneOf/1.explanation: Centre [x, y, z] of a {min, max} box: the midpoint of each min/max pair.
pitfalls: The box needs positive extent on all three axes; a flat box fails with FUNCTION_FAILED (use boundsCentre with six-number bounds for flat data).

/$defs/composition/anyOf/2/oneOf/1/prope.explanation: Registered function name; "boundsCentre3D" selects this calculation and fixes the argument and result contract.
/$defs/composition/anyOf/2/oneOf/1/prope.label: Function

/$defs/composition/anyOf/2/oneOf/1/prope.explanation: Arguments of boundsCentre3D: one required {min, max} box. Usually a literal object; the whole object may also come from a marker (for example $document to shared arguments) or from an $analytic whose samples are complete argument objects.
/$defs/composition/anyOf/2/oneOf/1/prope.label: Arguments

/$defs/composition/anyOf/2/oneOf/1/prope.explanation: Literal argument object of boundsCentre3D: required bounds.
Axis-aligned box given by its corners, {"min": [x, y, z], "max": [x, y, z]}, in the coordinate units of the data it describes. Its centre is returned.
/$defs/composition/anyOf/2/oneOf/1/prope.label: Bounds
/$defs/composition/anyOf/2/oneOf/1/prope.units: Coordinate units of the data (no unit conversion)

/$defs/composition/anyOf/2/oneOf/1/prope.explanation: Literal min/max box for boundsCentre3D; choose a marker to reuse a box from dimensions or from another function such as boundsUnion.
Lowest x, y and z of the box passed to boundsCentre3D; every component must be strictly less than the matching max component.
/$defs/composition/anyOf/2/oneOf/1/prope.label: Minimum corner
/$defs/composition/anyOf/2/oneOf/1/prope.units: Coordinate units of the data (no unit conversion)

/$defs/composition/anyOf/2/oneOf/1/prope.explanation: Literal [x, y, z] minimum corner for boundsCentre3D; choose a marker to take it from shared dimensions or another function result.
One component of the minimum corner for boundsCentre3D: x, y, then z.
Literal number for one component of the minimum corner (boundsCentre3D). Choose a composition marker instead to compute it, or $analytic to sweep it across states.
Highest x, y and z of the box passed to boundsCentre3D; every component must be strictly greater than the matching min component.
/$defs/composition/anyOf/2/oneOf/1/prope.label: Maximum corner
/$defs/composition/anyOf/2/oneOf/1/prope.units: Coordinate units of the data (no unit conversion)

/$defs/composition/anyOf/2/oneOf/1/prope.explanation: Literal [x, y, z] maximum corner for boundsCentre3D; choose a marker to take it from shared dimensions or another function result.
One component of the maximum corner for boundsCentre3D: x, y, then z.
Literal number for one component of the maximum corner (boundsCentre3D). Choose a composition marker instead to compute it, or $analytic to sweep it across states.

/$defs/composition/anyOf/2/oneOf/2.explanation: Grows or shrinks a {min, max} box by fractions of its own size: min - before x size and max + after x size on each axis. Returns a new {min, max} box, for example a domain with margins around a model.
pitfalls: The result must keep positive extent; large negative fractions fail with FUNCTION_FAILED.

/$defs/composition/anyOf/2/oneOf/2/prope.explanation: Registered function name; "boundsExtend" selects this calculation and fixes the argument and result contract.
/$defs/composition/anyOf/2/oneOf/2/prope.label: Function

/$defs/composition/anyOf/2/oneOf/2/prope.explanation: Arguments of boundsExtend: required bounds, optional before and after margin fractions. Usually a literal object; the whole object may also come from a marker (for example $document to shared arguments) or from an $analytic whose samples are complete argument objects.
/$defs/composition/anyOf/2/oneOf/2/prope.label: Arguments

/$defs/composition/anyOf/2/oneOf/2/prope.explanation: Literal argument object of boundsExtend: required bounds, optional before and after.
Axis-aligned box given by its corners, {"min": [x, y, z], "max": [x, y, z]}, in the coordinate units of the data it describes. This is the box to enlarge; margins are fractions of its size.
/$defs/composition/anyOf/2/oneOf/2/prope.label: Bounds
/$defs/composition/anyOf/2/oneOf/2/prope.units: Coordinate units of the data (no unit conversion)

/$defs/composition/anyOf/2/oneOf/2/prope.explanation: Literal min/max box for boundsExtend; choose a marker to reuse a box from dimensions or from another function such as boundsUnion.
Lowest x, y and z of the box passed to boundsExtend; every component must be strictly less than the matching max component.
/$defs/composition/anyOf/2/oneOf/2/prope.label: Minimum corner
/$defs/composition/anyOf/2/oneOf/2/prope.units: Coordinate units of the data (no unit conversion)

/$defs/composition/anyOf/2/oneOf/2/prope.explanation: Literal [x, y, z] minimum corner for boundsExtend; choose a marker to take it from shared dimensions or another function result.
One component of the minimum corner for boundsExtend: x, y, then z.
Literal number for one component of the minimum corner (boundsExtend). Choose a composition marker instead to compute it, or $analytic to sweep it across states.
Highest x, y and z of the box passed to boundsExtend; every component must be strictly greater than the matching min component.
/$defs/composition/anyOf/2/oneOf/2/prope.label: Maximum corner
/$defs/composition/anyOf/2/oneOf/2/prope.units: Coordinate units of the data (no unit conversion)

/$defs/composition/anyOf/2/oneOf/2/prope.explanation: Literal [x, y, z] maximum corner for boundsExtend; choose a marker to take it from shared dimensions or another function result.
One component of the maximum corner for boundsExtend: x, y, then z.
Literal number for one component of the maximum corner (boundsExtend). Choose a composition marker instead to compute it, or $analytic to sweep it across states.
Per-axis fractions of the box size added below min by boundsExtend: each component multiplies the box extent along that axis. Negative fractions shrink the box.
/$defs/composition/anyOf/2/oneOf/2/prope.label: Lower margins
pitfalls: These are fractions, not lengths: [0.1, 0, 0] adds 10 % of the x-size, not 0.1 units.

/$defs/composition/anyOf/2/oneOf/2/prope.explanation: Literal [x, y, z] lower margin fractions for boundsExtend.
Fraction of the box size added below min along one axis (x, y, then z) by boundsExtend.
Literal number for one lower margin fraction (boundsExtend). Choose a composition marker instead to compute it, or $analytic to sweep it across states.
Per-axis fractions of the box size added above max by boundsExtend: each component multiplies the box extent along that axis. Negative fractions shrink the box.
/$defs/composition/anyOf/2/oneOf/2/prope.label: Upper margins
pitfalls: These are fractions, not lengths: [0.1, 0, 0] adds 10 % of the x-size, not 0.1 units.

/$defs/composition/anyOf/2/oneOf/2/prope.explanation: Literal [x, y, z] upper margin fractions for boundsExtend.
Fraction of the box size added above max along one axis (x, y, then z) by boundsExtend.
Literal number for one upper margin fraction (boundsExtend). Choose a composition marker instead to compute it, or $analytic to sweep it across states.

/$defs/composition/anyOf/2/oneOf/3.explanation: Framing box for a side view of a model standing on a ground plane: extends the box like boundsExtend, sets its min z to floor, then raises its max z if needed so the height is at least the y-extent x aspect[1]/aspect[0]. Use it, for example, to frame a vehicle for a 16:9 side image.
pitfalls: floor must be at or below the extended box's min z, otherwise FUNCTION_FAILED.

/$defs/composition/anyOf/2/oneOf/3/prope.explanation: Registered function name; "boundsFrame" selects this calculation and fixes the argument and result contract.

/$defs/composition/anyOf/2/oneOf/3/prope.explanation: Arguments of boundsFrame: required bounds and floor, optional before, after and aspect. pitfalls: These are fractions, not lengths: [0.1, 0, 0] adds 10 % of the x-size, not 0.1 units.

z coordinate of the ground plane; it becomes the min z of the frame and must lie at or below the extended box.

/$defs/composition/anyOf/2/oneOf/3/prope.explanation: Literal number for the floor height (boundsFrame). Choose a composition marker instead to compute it, or $analytic to sweep it across states.
Image aspect ratio as [width, height]; only the ratio matters. The frame height is made at least the y-extent x height/width, as for a view along x.

/$defs/composition/anyOf/2/oneOf/3/prope.explanation: Literal [width, height] aspect pair for boundsFrame.

/$defs/composition/anyOf/2/oneOf/4.explanation: Size [dx, dy, dz] = max - min of a {min, max} box.
